root_cause.text: The `otx2_set_ringparam` function in the octeontx2-pf driver lacked validation of the user-supplied RX ring size (`rx_pending`), allowing values too small (below 16) that trigger an undefined shift-out-of-bounds error when passed to the `Q_SIZE` or `Q_COUNT` macros.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `if (ring->rx_pending < 16)` returning `-EINVAL`, and the commit message states it "fixes UBSAN shift-out-of-bounds errors when users passes small or zero ring sizes via ethtool -G".

commit d45d8979840d9c9ac93d3fe8cfc8e794b7228445
Author: Christina Jacob <cjacob@marvell.com>

    octeontx2-pf: Add basic ethtool support
    
    This patch adds ethtool support for
     - Driver stats, Tx/Rx perqueue and CGX LMAC stats
     - Set/show Rx/Tx queue count
     - Set/show Rx/Tx ring sizes

    Signed-off-by: Christina Jacob <cjacob@marvell.com>
    Signed-off-by: Sunil Goutham <sgoutham@marvell.co
bic_trace_step.reason: In `otx2_set_ringparam`, the RX ring size `rx_count` is taken directly from user-supplied `ring->rx_pending` and then used in `Q_COUNT(Q_SIZE(rx_count, 3))` without any lower-bound validation. The comment mentions 'Permitted lengths are 16 ...' but no check enforces a minimum of 16. This allows values below 16 that can cause undefined shift-out-of-bounds in the Q_SIZE/Q_COUNT macros. The TX side uses `clamp_t` to enforce a minimum, but RX does not, confirming the vulnerability.
